# Internal Read-Only MCP Server — Implementation Report

**Scope**: Part A's MCP half only. `env.manifest.json` itself is generated by
the parallel `env_manifest` workstream (`dv_harness/env_manifest.py` +
`dv_harness/schemas/env_manifest.schema.json`); this workstream builds the
read-only, fixed-5-verb server that consumes that file's output.

## What was built

`dv_harness/mcp/` (new subpackage, mirroring `dv_harness/uvm_generator/`'s
subpackage-with-`schemas/`-precedent, but without a nested `schemas/` dir of
its own — see the Reconciliation section below for why):

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `errors.py` | `McpError` / `McpNotFoundError` / `McpValidationError` / `McpUnknownVerbError` |
| `manifest_source.py` | The **only** function in this package that touches `env.manifest.json` on disk — `load_manifest()`, read-only (`Path.read_text()`, no write-mode `open()` anywhere) |
| `schema.py` | Fixed per-verb PARAM/RESULT JSON Schemas (draft 2020-12, `additionalProperties: false` throughout) + `validate_manifest()` against the **real**, now-landed `dv_harness/schemas/env_manifest.schema.json` |
| `verbs.py` | The 5 verbs' real logic — pure, framework-agnostic, JSON-in/JSON-out. `VERBS` dict + `dispatch()` — the single fixed-verb-only routing point |
| `regression_queries.py` | `query_regression`'s fixed SQL shapes (`latest`, `by_pattern`, `by_verdict`, `by_date_range`) over `evidence_db.EvidenceStore.query()` only |
| `runtime.py` | `ReadOnlyMcpContext` — the framework-agnostic `.call(verb, params)` entry point over real manifest/DB paths. No `mcp` SDK dependency. |
| `server.py` | Thin transport wrapper around the real, confirmed-installed `mcp` SDK (`mcp.server.mcpserver.MCPServer`) |

## Point 4 — which case applies (checked live, not guessed)

`import mcp` initially failed (`ModuleNotFoundError`; `pip show mcp` also
confirmed not installed) — so no MCP SDK was already established anywhere in
this repo/session. Per the task's own fallback instruction, `python -m pip
install mcp` was then run to check whether a real SDK is installable at all
in this environment (it is — outbound network access is available here). It
resolved and installed the **official Model Context Protocol Python SDK,
version 2.1.1** (latest at time of install; versions `1.0.0`–`1.29.1` and
`2.0.0`–`2.1.1` are all available on PyPI). In 2.1.1 the class earlier 1.x
releases called `FastMCP` was renamed `MCPServer`
(`mcp.server.mcpserver.MCPServer` — importing the old
`mcp.server.fastmcp.FastMCP` path under 2.1.1 raises a `ModuleNotFoundError`
whose own message states the rename and points at the SDK's migration
guide).

**Conclusion: case (b) applies, for real, not as a placeholder.** `server.py`
is a genuine thin wrapper around the real SDK's decorator-based tool API
(`MCPServer(...)`, `@server.tool()`, `server.run(transport="stdio")`), not a
hand-rolled JSON-line protocol pretending to be MCP. `verbs.py`/`runtime.py`
(the actual logic) have **no** dependency on `mcp` at all — they're plain
dicts in, dicts out — so the "function set first" half of the instruction is
also genuinely true: `server.py` could be deleted entirely and the other 6
files remain fully functional and fully tested.

`mcp>=2.1.1,<3` and `jsonschema>=4.0` were added to `requirements-harness.txt`
as optional dependencies (mirroring the existing `claude-code-sdk` entry's
own optional-dependency comment style). Neither is imported at
`dv_harness.mcp` package-import time — `duckdb`/`jsonschema`/`mcp` are all
imported lazily inside the functions that actually need them, matching
`evidence_db.py`'s own lazy-`duckdb`-import convention, so `import
dv_harness.mcp` never hard-fails on a machine missing one of those.

## Reconciliation — done, not just flagged

The task brief anticipated the manifest-generator workstream might still be
mid-flight, and explicitly allowed building against an *assumed* schema with
reconciliation flagged as a follow-up. That workstream's real schema (
`dv_harness/schemas/env_manifest.schema.json`) landed **during this same
session**, so a real reconciliation pass was done rather than deferred:

**What was originally assumed vs. what the real schema actually has:**

| Layer | Originally assumed | Real schema |
|---|---|---|
| `vip_config` | `status: AVAILABLE\|NOT_AVAILABLE`, `instances[].config` | `status: CAPTURED\|NOT_AVAILABLE`, `vip_instances[].config_fields` (flat string→string map) |
| `dut_facts` (RTL) | flat `dut_facts.modules[]` | `dut_facts.rtl.{status,reason,files[].modules[]}` — modules nested one level under each source file |
| `dut_facts` (registers) | flat `registers.entries[]` with a bare `address` field | `dut_facts.registers.{status: LOADED\|NOT_AVAILABLE, blocks[].{name, base_address, registers[].{address_offset, fields[]}}}` — register identity is `(block, register)`, address is base+offset, not a single absolute field |
| `env_topology` (hierarchy) | `components[].{path,type,is_active,parent}` | `component_hierarchy.{status,reason,components[].{full_name,type_name,is_active}}` — `is_active` is a real 3-value enum (`UVM_ACTIVE`/`UVM_PASSIVE`/`NOT_APPLICABLE`), not a bare bool |
| `env_topology` (config_db) | pre-paired `config_db_pairs[].{set_by[],get_by[]}` with a derivable `matched` bool | `config_db_trace.entries[]` — **raw, unpaired** SET/GET events (`kind`,`file`,`line`,`time`,`reporter`,`message`); `message` is deliberately left **opaque/unparsed** (`parse_confidence: "envelope_verified_message_opaque"`) |

`verbs.py`, `schema.py` (now validates directly against the real schema
file, no forked local copy), and `mcp_manifest_fixture.py` were all rewritten
to match the real shape exactly. `test_mcp_env_manifest_integration.py`
additionally builds a manifest through the **real generator**
(`env_manifest.generate_env_manifest()`) end-to-end and drives all 4
manifest-backed verbs against that real output — not just this package's own
hand-authored fixture — as the strongest available proof of fit.

### One genuine, still-open finding from this reconciliation

Part C's "a set with no get is direct evidence of a miswired vif" cannot
currently be computed as a per-field match/mismatch verdict, because the
real generator's `config_db_trace.entries[].message` is intentionally left
unparsed (`parse_confidence` says so explicitly — the message body's
internal field/context sub-format has never been verified against a live
UVM run). `get_topology` therefore returns the raw SET/GET entries
(filterable by `reporter` path prefix) plus honest **event counts**
(`config_db_set_event_count`/`config_db_get_event_count`), and deliberately
does **not** fabricate a `matched` boolean from unparsed text — doing so
would be exactly the kind of guess the Evidence Truth Rule forbids. Closing
this for real requires the generator's own `parse_config_db_trace_log()` to
gain structured field/context extraction from the message body first (a
change to that workstream's code, out of this task's scope) — noted here as
an explicit open gap, not silently worked around.

## Read-only enforcement (code-level, not just convention)

`dv_harness_tests/test_mcp_read_only_boundary.py`:
- **Static (AST) scan** over every `.py` file in `dv_harness/mcp/` (mirrors
  `test_vip_distill.py`'s own `test_module_does_not_import_orchestration_
  or_memory_modules()` scope-enforcement style): fails on any call to a
  fixed set of write-capable names (`write_text`, `unlink`, `rmtree`,
  `EvidenceStore`'s own real `insert_*` methods, `execute`/`executemany`/
  `commit`, or `open(..., mode=...)` with `w`/`a`/`x`/`+`), and on any
  `import shutil`/`import subprocess`.
- **Behavioral proof**: a real manifest file + a real `evidence.duckdb`
  (seeded via `EvidenceStore.insert_regression_verdict()`) are SHA-256
  hashed, then every verb is invoked through `ReadOnlyMcpContext` — success
  paths, a `NOT_FOUND` module lookup, an unknown verb, malformed params, and
  a SQL-injection-shaped `query_shape` string — and both hashes are asserted
  unchanged afterward. A second test independently re-confirms via real
  row-count queries (`EvidenceStore.query("SELECT count(*) FROM ...")`)
  across every table.
- `regression_queries.py`'s 4 SQL statements are individually asserted
  `SELECT`-only (no `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE`/`DROP`/`ALTER`/`CREATE`/`;`),
  and `run_query()` rejects any `query_shape` string outside the fixed set —
  including a literal `'; DROP TABLE regression_verdicts; --'` — with
  `McpValidationError`, never executing it.

7 files under `dv_harness_tests/`: `test_mcp_manifest_and_schema.py`,
`test_mcp_verbs.py`, `test_mcp_query_regression.py`,
`test_mcp_read_only_boundary.py`, `test_mcp_server_transport.py` (drives the

`mcp_manifest_fixture.py` (non-collected fixture-builder module, matching
`test_evidence_db.py`'s own cross-file `FIFO_FIXTURE` import convention).
